diagnosis.root_cause: The sed command 'sed -i 's/old/new/' notes.txt' failed on macOS with the error "sed: 1: \"notes.txt\n\": extra characters at the end of n command". This is a well-documented cross-platform compatibility issue: BSD sed (used on macOS) requires an explicit extension argument immediately after the -i flag (e.g., 'sed -i ''' or 'sed -i '.bak''), whereas GNU sed (Linux) allows -i without arguments or with a space before the extension. The workflow runs on a matrix including macos-latest but uses GNU sed syntax that only works on Linux.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Update the sed command in the workflow step to be compatible with both Linux and macOS. Replace 'sed -i 's/old/new/' notes.txt' with 'sed -i '' 's/old/new/' notes.txt' for macOS compatibility, or use a conditional approach that detects the OS and applies the appropriate syntax. Alternatively, use a cross-platform tool like perl: 'perl -i -pe 's/old/new/' notes.txt'.
